faq.subtitle: Everything you need to know about the 2026 edition.

items.q: When will the 2026 edition be published?
items.a:
The 2026 edition of Algeria Banking Index is expected to be published in September 2026.

Subscribers will be notified as soon as the study is available.

items.q: What will be the scope of the 2026 edition?
items.a: The 2026 edition will cover 21 banks operating in Algeria. It will focus primarily on comparing 2024–2025 performance, complemented by an analysis of trends observed over the 2023–2025 period.

The study will offer a consolidated analysis of the Algerian banking sector, comparisons between public and private banks, individual analyses of 21 institutions, as well as rankings and benchmarks by indicator.

This edition will also be enriched with new insights on off-balance sheet items, workforce, banking network, and operational performance.

It will also include a section dedicated to banking user experience — mobile app, web e-banking, and branch services — through the ABIX 2026 Barometer.

items.q: What does the early subscription guarantee?
items.a:
Early subscription allows you to reserve the 2026 edition before its publication and benefit from a 10% preferential rate.

Upon publication, deliverables corresponding to the subscribed pack will be made available to the subscriber.

Yes. Any subscription registered by August 31, 2026 at 23:59 (Algerian time) benefits from the early subscription rate.

This rate remains guaranteed until the study is delivered.

items.q: What are the different offer levels?
Can I receive a pro forma invoice?
items.a: Yes. Upon request, Tadjeddine & Partners can issue a pro forma invoice for the selected pack to facilitate your organization's internal procurement procedure.

items.q: Can I subscribe for multiple users?
items.a:
Yes.

The Essential Pack is designed for 1 user.

The Pro Pack allows access for up to 3 users belonging to the same entity.

The Corporate Executive Pack allows access for up to 20 users belonging to the same entity.

items.q: Are the 2024 data identical to those in the previous edition?
items.a:
Not necessarily.

Some banks have performed reclassifications or restatements of certain financial line items in subsequent publications.

To ensure maximum consistency with 2025 data, the 2026 edition uses the most recent revised 2024 data available.

These numbers replace those used in the previous edition where necessary.

items.q: Will the Banking Services Barometer influence financial results or bank rankings?
items.a:
No.

The Banking Services Barometer is a distinct section dedicated to user experience and satisfaction regarding banking services — mobile app, web e-banking, and branch services.

Its results do not alter the financial data of institutions.

They will be presented separately, along with a description of the methodology used and representativeness information.

items.q: Will the study feature perspectives from bank executives and experts?
items.a:
The 2026 edition also plans to host signed contributions from bank executives and experts, subject to editorial confirmation.

These contributions will be clearly distinguished from Algeria Banking Index's independent analysis.

They will not enter into indicator calculations, rankings, or independent conclusions.

items.q: Is the 2025 edition included in the 2026 subscription?
items.a:
No.

The 2025 edition remains an independent publication and can be acquired separately.

For organizations wishing to obtain both 2025 and 2026 editions, a bundled proposal can be arranged upon request.

items.q: What happens if the publication date changes?
items.a:
Subscribers will be notified of any changes to the publication timeline.

The subscription will remain valid and the preferential rate secured before August 31, 2026 will remain guaranteed.

items.q: Can I request a presentation or a custom benchmark?
items.a:
Yes.

The Corporate Executive Pack includes a briefing session and a custom benchmark.

Additional advisory services, such as a presentation to a board of directors or an in-depth analysis, can also be offered separately.

hero.title: Study Methodology
hero.subtitle: A structured approach to collect, consolidate, compare, and interpret financial, operational, and public data relating to the Algerian banking sector.
hero.introText: Algeria Banking Index studies rely on the methodical use of publicly available information, its harmonisation, and comparative analysis. The objective is to provide a consistent reading of performance, trends, and positioning across covered institutions.

disclaimerBox.title: What the methodology does NOT constitute
disclaimerBox.p1: The published analyses do not constitute a credit rating, a prudential rating, a solvency certification, a financial audit, or an investment recommendation.
disclaimerBox.p2: They rely on publicly available information and a comparative methodology proprietary to Algeria Banking Index studies.

approach.title: Our 6-Step Analytical Approach
approach.description: Algeria Banking Index studies rest on structured collection of publicly available information, followed by consolidation, consistency verification, comparison, and interpretation.

steps.title: Scope & Data Collection
steps.body: Identification and extraction of information published by banks and available institutional sources: financial statements, annual reports, and other relevant financial or operational disclosures.

steps.title: Consolidation, Consistency & Restatements
steps.body: Data consistency verification, reconciliation of aggregates, and standardized treatment of information across institutions and fiscal years.
steps.note: When banks subsequently publish restated or reclassified historical data, studies adopt the latest available revised data to preserve comparative consistency.

steps.title: Definition & Standardization of Indicators
steps.body: Standardized definition of indicators used, distinguishing between stock data, flow data, and financial ratios.
steps.note: Calculations cover growth, profitability, efficiency, market shares, and indicators enabling the comparison of institutional trajectories.

steps.title: Sector Comparisons & Positioning
steps.body: Analysis of sector aggregates, public vs. private bank comparisons, evolution of market shares, and relative positioning of institutions across studied indicators.
steps.badge: Methodological Principle: Comparisons are conducted on an identical methodological basis across all covered institutions.

steps.title: Individual Analyses & Operational Dimensions
steps.body: Each institution undergoes an individual review of its evolution, positioning, and core performance indicators.
steps.note: Subject to data availability and comparability, analysis may also integrate operational metrics such as off-balance sheet commitments, workforce, branch network, and operational productivity.

steps.title: Review, Analysis & Interpretation
steps.body: Consolidated data is analyzed and interpreted by Mr. Rachid Sekak and Tadjeddine & Partners to identify meaningful shifts, industry trends, and factors explaining observed trajectories.
steps.note: Factual findings, calculations, and interpretations are distinguished wherever possible in the study deliverables.

revisions.title: Historical Data and Revisions
revisions.p1: Historical data may evolve over time.
revisions.p2: Some banks may perform reclassifications or restatements for previous financial years in subsequent publications.
revisions.p3: When a revised figure is published by an institution, Algeria Banking Index may substitute this figure for the one used in an earlier edition to maintain consistent comparative series.
revisions.p4: Numbers in a new edition may therefore occasionally differ from those in a previous edition without implying an error.

ebanking.title: Specific Methodology for the Banking Services Barometer
ebanking.p1: The Banking Services Barometer constitutes a complementary and independent pillar alongside financial analysis.
ebanking.p2: It is based on a survey of banking service users to measure satisfaction levels and perceptions of offered services.
ebanking.p3: Barometer results are presented separately from financial indicators. They do not enter into financial ratio calculations or accounting-based rankings.
ebanking.p4: Published results specify respondent sample size, data collection period, response distribution, and representativeness parameters.

contributions.title: Editorial Contributions
contributions.p1: Certain editions may feature signed contributions from bank executives or industry experts.
contributions.p2: These contributions are clearly identified and separate from analysis produced by Algeria Banking Index.
contributions.p3: They reflect the authors' opinions and do not enter into calculations, comparisons, or independent study conclusions.

sources.title: Sources and Limitations
sources.p1: Analyses are prepared from public information available at the closing date of each edition.
sources.p2: Data availability, detail level, and presentation format may vary across institutions.
sources.p3: When data is unavailable or cannot be homogenously compared, it may be excluded from specific indicators or flagged explicitly.

why.title: Why this analysis?
why.paragraph1: The availability of financial information represents an important dimension in observing a banking institution.
why.paragraph2: Beyond analyzing financial performance, ABIX also examines how institutions make their financial statements and activity reports accessible to the general public.

methodology.subtitle: A standardized assessment measuring the public accessibility of two benchmark documents on official websites.

methodology.globalScoreFormula: Financial Statements + Activity Report = score out of 6
methodology.globalScoreNote: The score aims to measure the digital availability of the observed information, and not the intrinsic quality of the published content.
methodology.disclaimerText: This analysis focuses exclusively on information identified on the official websites of the institutions during the review conducted by ABIX. The absence of an identified document on a website does not necessarily mean that it has not been produced, submitted to competent authorities, or distributed through other channels. The score measures the online availability and timeliness of accessible information. It constitutes neither an assessment of the intrinsic quality of accounts, nor an evaluation of regulatory compliance, governance, or financial strength.

items.short_definition: Measures the overall balance sheet scale of a bank by summing all its assets as of December 31.
items.detailed_definition: Total Assets represents total closing accounting assets. In ABIX Data Explorer, it serves as the benchmark aggregate for market share calculations, bank size grouping, and sector weighting.
items.formula: Total Bilan = Caisse & Banques centrales + Titres & Bons du Trésor + Crédits clientèle + Autres actifs
items.interpretation: An indicator of relative size and institutional presence. It does not by itself measure profitability or solvency.
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition, 20-bank scope: Consolidated sector total assets of approx. 18,500 billion DZD, ~87% held by public banks.
items.example_vintage: Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025, périmètre de 20 banques

items.short_definition: Total financial resources entrusted to the bank by customers in checking, term, or savings accounts.
items.detailed_definition: Customer deposits aggregate demand, term, savings, and collateral deposits from households, corporates, and institutions. They represent the primary funding base for intermediation.
items.formula: Dépôts = Dépôts à vue + Dépôts à terme + Livrets d'épargne + Autres dépôts clientèle
items.interpretation: Measures funding capture and customer loyalty. A high share of demand deposits lowers overall cost of funding.
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition, 20-bank scope: Total deposit volume of 14,200 billion DZD.
items.example_vintage: Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025, périmètre de 20 banques

items.short_definition: Total outstanding financings and credit facilities granted to the economy (enterprises, professionals, retail).
items.detailed_definition: Represents total gross lending facilities extended by the bank across overdrafts, corporate working capital, equipment loans, mortgages, and consumer credit.
items.formula: Crédits = Crédits d'exploitation + Crédits d'investissement + Crédits immobiliers + Crédits aux particuliers
items.interpretation: Reflects the bank's active contribution to economic financing and counterparty risk exposure.
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition, 20-bank scope: Gross customer loans of 11,100 billion DZD.
items.example_vintage: Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025, périmètre de 20 banques

items.short_definition: Stable resources belonging to shareholders, comprising share capital, reserves, and retained earnings.
items.detailed_definition: Accounting Equity represents the net book value on the balance sheet. It acts as the financial cushion against unexpected losses. ABIX note: book equity is distinct from regulatory capital (Tier 1/Tier 2) under Bank of Algeria Regulation 2014-01.
items.formula: Fonds Propres = Capital social + Primes d'émission + Réserves + Report à nouveau + Résultat net
items.interpretation: A high equity buffer enhances financial autonomy and shock absorption capacity.
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition, 20-bank scope: Sector accounting equity of 2,450 billion DZD.
items.example_vintage: Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025, périmètre de 20 banques

items.short_definition: Gross banking operational margin measuring revenue creation before operating expenses.
items.detailed_definition: NBI is the banking equivalent of gross revenue. It consists of net interest income, net fee and commission income, and net trading and FX gains.
items.formula: PNB = (Intérêts reçus − Intérêts versés) + (Commissions reçues − Commissions payées) + Gains de change & titres
items.interpretation: Reflects commercial dynamism and the bank's capacity to monetize intermediation and payment services.
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition, 20-bank scope: Sector Net Banking Income of 430 billion DZD.
items.example_vintage: Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025, périmètre de 20 banques

items.short_definition: Surplus generated by core operations after deducting general operating expenses and depreciation.
items.detailed_definition: GOI measures the pure operational profitability before credit risk provisions and non-recurring items. It equals NBI minus operating costs and depreciation.
items.formula: RBE = Produit Net Bancaire − Frais généraux d'exploitation − Dotations aux amortissements
items.interpretation: A solid and growing GOI demonstrates disciplined cost management relative to commercial revenue.
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition, 20-bank scope: Sector Gross Operating Income of 245 billion DZD.
items.example_vintage: Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025, périmètre de 20 banques

items.short_definition: Bottom-line profit or loss attributable to the bank after credit risk provisions and corporate taxes.
items.detailed_definition: Net Income represents final net earnings after cost of risk (loan provisions), corporate income tax (IBS), and non-operating gains/losses.
items.formula: Résultat Net = RBE − Coût net du risque (Provisions nettes) + Résultat exceptionnel − Impôts (IBS)
items.interpretation: Ultimate measure of financial return. It directly builds equity through retained earnings or funds dividend distribution.
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition, 20-bank scope: Consolidated sector net profit of 185 billion DZD.
items.example_vintage: Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025, périmètre de 20 banques

items.short_definition: Outstanding stock of sovereign debt securities issued by the Algerian Treasury held by the bank.
items.detailed_definition: Includes short-term and medium/long-term sovereign paper issued by the State Treasury. In Algeria, Treasury paper represents a core asset allocation pillar. Prudential note: Sovereign exposures may benefit from preferential prudential treatment in accordance with applicable regulatory frameworks and qualifying criteria.
items.formula: Bons du Trésor = Bons du Trésor à Court Terme + Bons du Trésor à Moyen et Long Terme + Titres assimilés
items.interpretation: A high share reflects a conservative asset allocation strategy or surplus liquidity invested in sovereign debt.
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition, 20-bank scope: Sector Treasury securities portfolio of 3,800 billion DZD.
items.example_vintage: Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025, périmètre de 20 banques

items.short_definition: Ratio of net income to closing equity, measuring financial return generated for shareholders.
items.detailed_definition: In ABIX Data Explorer, standard ROE is calculated by dividing net profit by closing book equity as of December 31. It measures the return generated on invested capital. Methodology note: for multi-year dynamic analyses, refer also to ROAE based on average equity.
items.formula: ROE = (Résultat Net ÷ Fonds Propres de clôture) × 100
items.interpretation: A higher ROE reflects strong financial profitability, but must be evaluated alongside leverage and underlying risk profile.
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition, 20-bank scope: Sector median ROE of 9.8%, ranging from 3.5% to over 22%.
items.example_vintage: Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025, périmètre de 20 banques

items.short_definition: Ratio of net income to average equity between the beginning and end of the fiscal year.
items.detailed_definition: ROAE neutralizes intra-year capital variations (equity injections, dividend payouts). It provides a refined economic measurement of returns on capital employed throughout the year.
items.formula: ROAE = [Résultat Net ÷ ((Fonds Propres t + Fonds Propres t-1) ÷ 2)] × 100
items.interpretation: Preferred for rigorous multi-year analysis when material intra-year equity changes occur.
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition, constant scope: For 12B DZD profit and equity moving from 100B to 120B DZD, ROAE is 10.9% (vs 10.0% closing ROE).
items.example_vintage: Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025, périmètre constant

items.short_definition: Ratio of net income to closing total assets, measuring overall asset productivity.
items.detailed_definition: In ABIX Data Explorer, ROA is computed on closing balance sheet assets as of December 31. It measures the bank's ability to generate earnings per unit of asset managed.
items.formula: ROA = (Résultat Net ÷ Total Bilan de clôture) × 100
items.interpretation: A key indicator of operational profitability. In banking, a ROA above 1.5% reflects strong underlying earning power.
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition, 20-bank scope: Sector average ROA of 1.12%, with peaks above 2.5% among private specialized institutions.
items.example_vintage: Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025, périmètre de 20 banques

items.short_definition: Ratio of net income to average total assets across the fiscal year.
items.detailed_definition: ROAA smooths out intra-year balance sheet expansions (rapid deposit growth, refinancing). It represents the academic standard for measuring asset efficiency over time.
items.formula: ROAA = [Résultat Net ÷ ((Total Bilan t + Total Bilan t-1) ÷ 2)] × 100
items.interpretation: International benchmark standard to neutralize year-end balance sheet seasonality.
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition, constant scope: 5B DZD profit on assets expanding from 400B to 500B DZD: ROAA is 1.11% (vs 1.00% closing ROA).
items.example_vintage: Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025, périmètre constant

items.short_definition: Share of Net Banking Income consumed by operating overhead and depreciation.
items.detailed_definition: The CIR measures operational efficiency. A lower ratio indicates higher operational productivity in converting revenues to gross profit. In ABIX scoring models, it operates as an inverted metric (lower is better).
items.formula: Coefficient d'Exploitation = [(Frais généraux + Amortissements) ÷ Produit Net Bancaire] × 100
items.interpretation: A lower ratio reflects lean operations. A ratio above 60-65% indicates elevated structural overhead.
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition, 20-bank scope: Sector median CIR of 43.5%, top-tier efficient banks standing below 35%.
items.example_vintage: Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025, périmètre de 20 banques

items.short_definition: Ratio of net interest income earned to interest-earning assets.
items.detailed_definition: NIM measures the core spread profitability of financial intermediation. ABIX methodology note: Where detailed average earning assets are not homogeneously reported across all banks, ABIX applies the NBI / Total Assets proxy ratio.
items.formula: NIM théorique = (Marge d'intérêt nette ÷ Actifs productifs moyens) × 100 | Proxy ABIX = (PNB ÷ Total Bilan) × 100
items.interpretation: A healthy margin reflects loan pricing discipline combined with low-cost customer funding.
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition, 20-bank scope: Sector average NBI / Total Assets proxy of 2.35%.
items.example_vintage: Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025, périmètre de 20 banques

items.short_definition: Percentage of Net Banking Income successfully converted into final net profit.
items.detailed_definition: Net Profit Margin assesses the overall capacity of the bank to retain revenues after operating costs, loan impairment provisions, and corporate taxes.
items.formula: Marge Nette sur PNB = (Résultat Net ÷ Produit Net Bancaire) × 100
items.interpretation: A higher margin indicates a highly profitable and resilient operating model.
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition, 20-bank scope: Sector median net profit margin of 42.8%.
items.example_vintage: Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025, périmètre de 20 banques

items.term: GOI to Net Profit Conversion Rate
items.short_definition: Share of Gross Operating Income retained as net profit after credit risk provisions and taxes.
items.detailed_definition: Measures the resilience of operational income against provisions and taxes. A conversion rate near 100% indicates that gross operating profit was not impaired by credit loss charges.
items.formula: Taux de Conversion RBE → RN = (Résultat Net ÷ RBE) × 100
items.interpretation: A sharp drop signals an acceleration in credit loss provisioning or non-operating write-offs.
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition, 20-bank scope: Sector median conversion rate of 75.5%.
items.example_vintage: Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025, périmètre de 20 banques

items.short_definition: Ratio of regulatory capital to risk-weighted assets (credit, market, operational risks).
items.detailed_definition: Measures the prudential capital cushion against risk-weighted assets. Algerian regulatory framework: Pursuant to Bank of Algeria Regulation No. 2014-01 of February 16, 2014, mandatory requirements are: 1) Minimum global capital adequacy ratio: at least 9.5% of risk-weighted assets; 2) Tier 1 capital: at least 7.0% of risk-weighted assets. ABIX comfort benchmark: An indicative comfort range in the local market is generally situated between 14% and 18%.
items.formula: Ratio de Solvabilité = (Fonds Propres Réglementaires Globaux ÷ Actifs Pondérés par les Risques) × 100
items.interpretation: A ratio exceeding the 9.5% legal minimum confirms regulatory compliance. A very high ratio (> 20%) ensures maximum safety but may signal under-deployed credit capacity.
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition: Sector average CAR estimated at ~16.2%, well above the 9.5% regulatory floor.
items.example_vintage: Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025, périmètre bancaire algérien

items.short_definition: Ratio of highest quality core capital (paid-up capital and retained earnings) to risk-weighted assets.
items.detailed_definition: Tier 1 ratio evaluates the bank's capacity to absorb immediate losses on a going-concern basis. Algerian regulation: BA Regulation No. 2014-01 mandates a minimum Tier 1 capital ratio of 7.0% of risk-weighted assets.
items.formula: Ratio Tier 1 = (Fonds Propres de Base Tier 1 ÷ Actifs Pondérés par les Risques) × 100
items.interpretation: A strong Tier 1 ratio ensures long-term viability without requiring emergency capital injections in stress scenarios.
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition: Average Tier 1 ratio of major Algerian banks estimated above 13.5%, compliant with regulations.
items.example_vintage: Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025, banques algériennes

items.short_definition: Proportion of loans with payments past due (typically > 90 days) or presenting recognized default risk.
items.detailed_definition: The NPL ratio is the primary indicator of asset quality. It measures impaired and doubtful loans relative to total gross credit portfolio. In ABIX, it is an inverted metric (lower is better).
items.formula: Taux NPL = (Créances Non Performantes brutes ÷ Encours Total des Crédits bruts) × 100
items.interpretation: A low ratio reflects strict underwriting standards and efficient recovery. A high ratio necessitates heavy provisioning that weighs on profit.
items.example: Indicative sector data: Average sector NPL ratio around 10-12%, with marked divergence between public banks (legacy exposures) and private subsidiaries (often < 5%).
items.example_vintage: Données sectorielles indicatives, Édition ABIX 2025

items.short_definition: Ratio of accumulated loan loss provisions to total non-performing loans.
items.detailed_definition: Assesses the degree of balance sheet protection against anticipated credit losses on impaired loans. A high coverage ratio means that the bulk of bad debt is already provisioned.
items.formula: Taux de Couverture = (Stock de Provisions pour Dépréciation ÷ Encours Brut des NPL) × 100
items.interpretation: A coverage ratio above 70-80% is widely regarded as a prudential comfort benchmark in emerging banking markets.
items.example: Methodological example: For 50B DZD in impaired loans with 40B DZD in cumulative provisions, the coverage ratio stands at 80.0%.
items.example_vintage: Exemple méthodologique calibré

items.term: Provisioning Effort to Loans (Cost of Risk Proxy)
items.short_definition: Annual net loan loss provisioning charges divided by total loan portfolio.
items.detailed_definition: Serves as the direct proxy for cost of risk in ABIX Data Explorer. It measures the annual P&L charge required to absorb credit deterioration across the loan book.
items.formula: Effort de Provisionnement = (Dotations Nettes aux Provisions ÷ Encours des Prêts) × 100
items.interpretation: A low and steady provisioning effort indicates disciplined underwriting and low default incidence.
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition, 20-bank scope: Sector median provisioning effort of 0.55% of total loans.
items.example_vintage: Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025, périmètre de 20 banques

items.term: Provision Burden on Gross Operating Income
items.short_definition: Percentage of Gross Operating Income consumed by net credit loss provisioning charges.
items.detailed_definition: Measures the proportion of operating income absorbed by credit loss provisioning. ABIX note: An increase may reflect deteriorating borrower quality or a proactive, conservative provisioning stance.
items.formula: Pression Provisions / RBE = (Dotations Nettes aux Provisions ÷ RBE) × 100
items.interpretation: A ratio below 20-25% preserves the bulk of operating surplus for net bottom-line profit.
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition, 20-bank scope: Sector median provision burden on GOI of 18.4%.
items.example_vintage: Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025, périmètre de 20 banques

items.short_definition: Share of the balance sheet financed by book equity.
items.detailed_definition: Direct accounting metric of balance sheet equity backing. ABIX note: This is a simplified accounting capitalization ratio and does not substitute for regulatory solvency ratios based on risk-weighted assets (RWA).
items.formula: Fonds Propres / Total Bilan = (Fonds Propres Comptables ÷ Total Bilan) × 100
items.interpretation: A high ratio (> 12-15%) indicates strong capital backing and high financial safety.
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition, 20-bank scope: Sector average ratio of 13.2%, reflecting strong equity backing.
items.example_vintage: Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025, périmètre de 20 banques

items.short_definition: Number of times total assets exceed the bank's book equity.
items.detailed_definition: Measures balance sheet asset scale relative to equity backing. ABIX note: This is a simplified accounting leverage multiple and does not constitute the Basel III regulatory leverage ratio (which includes off-balance sheet items and prudential deductions).
items.formula: Levier Comptable = Total Bilan ÷ Fonds Propres Comptables
items.interpretation: A moderate leverage (6x to 9x) ensures strong safety. Elevated leverage (> 15x) heightens solvency vulnerability.
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition, 20-bank scope: Sector median accounting leverage of 7.6x.
items.example_vintage: Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025, périmètre de 20 banques

items.short_definition: Proportion of customer deposits that is actively transformed and lent out as customer loans.
items.detailed_definition: The LDR measures the bank's financial intermediation depth. It compares net loans to customer deposits. A balanced ratio ensures that lending is funded by stable customer deposits without excessive reliance on wholesale funding.
items.formula: Ratio Prêts / Dépôts = (Crédits Nets à la Clientèle ÷ Dépôts de la Clientèle) × 100
items.interpretation: An LDR between 70% and 90% indicates balanced intermediation. Below 60%, resources are under-deployed; above 100%, the bank relies on external funding.
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition, 20-bank scope: Sector average LDR of 78.2%, reflecting solid deposit backing.
items.example_vintage: Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025, périmètre de 20 banques

items.short_definition: Percentage of total bank assets allocated to customer loans.
items.detailed_definition: Reflects the bank's asset allocation profile. A high loan share characterizes a commercial lending bank, whereas a lower share indicates a sovereign paper or cash management focus.
items.formula: Prêts / Total Bilan = (Encours des Crédits Clientèle ÷ Total Bilan) × 100
items.interpretation: Measures core lending intensity. A higher ratio correlates with greater revenue sensitivity to private credit risk.
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition, 20-bank scope: Sector average loan share of total assets of 60.0%.
items.example_vintage: Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025, périmètre de 20 banques

items.short_definition: Percentage of total assets invested in sovereign debt securities issued by the Algerian State Treasury.
items.detailed_definition: Measures the sovereign allocation weight within the asset base. Historically in Algeria, public banks hold material Treasury securities volumes from balance sheet restructuring and liquidity placements.
items.formula: BDT / Total Bilan = (Encours des Bons du Trésor ÷ Total Bilan) × 100
items.interpretation: A high ratio secures liquidity and sovereign coupon income, but may reflect relative crowding-out of private sector credit.
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition, 20-bank scope: Average Treasury securities share of 20.5% of sector total assets.
items.example_vintage: Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025, périmètre de 20 banques

items.short_definition: Percentage of total balance sheet funded by customer deposits.
items.detailed_definition: Measures the bank's structural reliance on customer deposits compared to other funding sources (equity, interbank borrowing, bond issues).
items.formula: Dépôts / Total Bilan = (Dépôts de la Clientèle ÷ Total Bilan) × 100
items.interpretation: A share above 75-80% characterizes a traditional commercial retail banking model with a granular, stable funding base.
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition, 20-bank scope: Sector average deposit share of 76.8% of total liabilities.
items.example_vintage: Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025, périmètre de 20 banques

items.short_definition: Portion of total assets not accounted for by customer loans and Treasury securities.
items.detailed_definition: In ABIX balance sheet allocation models, Other Assets is the residual balance (Total Assets minus Loans minus Treasury Securities), encompassing cash, central bank reserves, interbank placements, fixed assets, and sundry accounts.
items.formula: Autres Actifs = Total Bilan − Prêts clientèle − Bons du Trésor
items.interpretation: Enables full 100% balance sheet decomposition (Loans + Treasury + Other = 100%). A negative value flags potential data inconsistency.
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition, 20-bank scope: Sector other assets volume of ~3,600 billion DZD (~19.5% of total assets).
items.example_vintage: Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025, périmètre de 20 banques

items.short_definition: Bank capacity to withstand severe 30-day acute liquidity stress.
items.detailed_definition: Compares high-quality liquid assets (HQLA) readily convertible to central bank cash against estimated 30-day net cash outflows under severe stress. Standard requirement: Minimum 100%.
items.formula: LCR = (Stock d'Actifs Liquides de Haute Qualité HQLA ÷ Sorties Nettes de Trésorerie à 30j) × 100
items.interpretation: An LCR above 100% ensures the bank holds sufficient liquid buffers to withstand deposit run-offs without emergency aid.
items.example: Normative example: For 120B DZD in HQLA and 80B DZD in 30-day modeled net outflows, LCR is 150% (exceeding 100% minimum).
items.example_vintage: Exemple méthodologique normatif Bâle III

items.short_definition: Measures structural alignment between stable available funding and required illiquid assets over a 1-year horizon.
items.detailed_definition: NSFR limits excessive reliance on short-term wholesale funding to finance long-term assets. It divides available stable funding (ASF) by required stable funding (RSF). Prudential standard: Minimum 100%.
items.formula: NSFR = (Montant de Financement Stable Disponible ASF ÷ Financement Stable Exigé RSF) × 100
items.interpretation: An NSFR above 100% confirms that long-term illiquid assets are funded by durable, sticky equity and deposits.
items.example: Methodological example: 200B DZD ASF covering 160B DZD RSF yields a solid 125% NSFR.
items.regulatory_threshold: >= 100 % (Standard prudentiel de financement stable Bâle III)
items.example_vintage: Exemple méthodologique normatif Bâle III

items.short_definition: Sum of all observed values divided by the total number of banks in the sample.
items.detailed_definition: The arithmetic mean measures central tendency. In ABIX Data Explorer, it is computed strictly on available numeric observations (excluding nulls). It can be sensitive to extreme outliers in highly concentrated banking systems.
items.formula: Moyenne = (Σ Xi) ÷ N (pour i = 1 à N)
items.interpretation: Provides the overall market level, but should be compared with the median to assess distributional skewness.
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition, 20-bank scope: Sector mean ROE is 11.4% vs median of 9.8% (positive skew driven by top performers).
items.example_vintage: Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025, périmètre de 20 banques

items.short_definition: Value separating the ordered sample of banks into two equal halves (50% above, 50% below).
items.detailed_definition: The median is ABIX's primary robust central tendency metric because it is fully resistant to extreme outliers and public bank scale distortions. Exact formulation: 1) For an odd number N of banks (e.g. 21 banks in 2026): Median = central value at rank (N+1)/2; 2) For an even number N of banks (e.g. 20 banks in 2025): Median = arithmetic average of the two central values at ranks N/2 and (N/2)+1.
items.formula: Si N impair : Médiane = X_((N+1)/2) | Si N pair : Médiane = (X_(N/2) + X_(N/2 + 1)) ÷ 2
items.formula_latex: \\text{Médiane} = \\begin{cases} X_{\\frac{N+1}{2}} & \\text{si } N \\text{ impair} \\\\ \\frac{X_{\\frac{N}{2}} + X_{\\frac{N}{2}+1}}{2} & \\text{si } N \\text{ pair} \\end{cases}
items.interpretation: Represents the performance of a typical median bank in Algeria without weighting bias towards giant public banks.
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition (20 banks, even N): Median CIR is the average of the 10th bank (43.2%) and 11th bank (43.8%), exactly 43.5%.
items.example_vintage: Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025, périmètre de 20 banques

items.short_definition: Three statistical thresholds (Q1=25th, Q2=50th=Median, Q3=75th percentile) dividing the sector into four equal cohorts.
items.detailed_definition: Descriptive quartile thresholds: 1) Q1 = 25th percentile; 2) Q2 = 50th percentile = Median; 3) Q3 = 75th percentile. ABIX engine computes percentiles using linear interpolation (N-1)*p. ABIX Performance Note: In ABIX executive restitution, the 'Q1' label is awarded to the top 25% best performers (e.g. highest ROE or lowest Cost-to-Income).
items.formula: Q1 = P25 (interpolation linéaire) | Q2 = Médiane (P50) | Q3 = P75 (interpolation linéaire)
items.formula_latex: Q_1 = P_{25},\\quad Q_2 = P_{50} = \\text{Médiane},\\quad Q_3 = P_{75}
items.interpretation: Positions each bank objectively within its peer distribution tier without mean-driven distortion.
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition, sector ROE (20 banks): Q1 = 6.2%, Q2 = 9.8%, Q3 = 14.5%. Banks with ROE > 14.5% belong to the top performance quartile Q1.
items.example_vintage: Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025, périmètre de 20 banques

items.short_definition: Statistical measurement of data dispersion around the arithmetic mean.
items.detailed_definition: Quantifies the homogeneity or dispersion of banking metrics across institutions. Statistical note: In an approximately normal distribution, ~68% of observations fall within ±1σ and ~95% within ±2σ of the mean.
items.formula: Écart-type (σ) = √ [ (1 ÷ N) × Σ (Xi − X̄)² ]
items.interpretation: Evaluates mean representativeness and identifies outlier banks lying beyond 2 standard deviations.
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition, 20-bank scope: For a mean ROE of 11.4% with sector σ = 5.2%, the range [6.2% - 16.6%] encompasses the core bank cohort.
items.example_vintage: Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025, périmètre de 20 banques

items.short_definition: Ratio of standard deviation to arithmetic mean, expressing relative dispersion as a normalized percentage.
items.detailed_definition: The CV is a dimensionless metric enabling direct dispersion comparison across financial indicators with different units or scales (e.g. comparing deposits dispersion in billion DZD with ROE dispersion in %).
items.formula: Coefficient de Variation (CV) = (Écart-type σ ÷ Moyenne arithmétique X̄) × 100
items.interpretation: CV < 15% indicates strong sector homogeneity. CV > 30-50% indicates high dispersion and structural polarization.
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition: Cost-to-Income CV is 24% (moderate), whereas Total Assets CV reaches 145% (extreme scale skewness).
items.example_vintage: Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025, périmètre de 20 banques

items.short_definition: Constant annual rate at which a metric would have grown from its base year to final year over n periods.
items.detailed_definition: CAGR smooths out year-to-year volatility through geometric progression. In ABIX Data Explorer, CAGR is used in the Growth scoring pillar (25% weight each on Assets, Loans, NBI, and Net Profit).
items.formula: CAGR = [ (Valeur Finale ÷ Valeur Initiale)^(1 ÷ n) − 1 ] × 100
items.interpretation: Provides a standardized, fair multi-year growth comparison across institutions of varying scale.
items.example: 2021-2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition (constant scope): Sector loans expanded from 8,500B to 11,100B DZD over 3 years, representing a CAGR of +9.3% per annum.
items.example_vintage: Données 2021-2024, Édition ABIX 2025, périmètre constant

items.short_definition: Percentage change of a financial metric between period t and the preceding period t-1.
items.detailed_definition: Measures annual metric expansion or contraction. In ABIX Data Explorer, for indicators already expressed as percentages (e.g. ROE, CIR), the variation is strictly tracked in percentage points (point_change).
items.formula: Pour agrégats (Mds DZD) : YoY = [(Vt − Vt-1) ÷ Vt-1] × 100 | Pour ratios (%) : Δ = Vt − Vt-1 (en points)
items.interpretation: Identifies trend shifts, commercial accelerations, or abrupt year-over-year decelerations.
items.example: 2024 vs 2023 data, ABIX 2025 edition: Sector NBI grew by +8.2% YoY, while average ROE gained +0.6 percentage points.
items.example_vintage: Données 2024 vs 2023, Édition ABIX 2025

items.short_definition: Index normalizing base year metric to 100 to visually compare growth trajectories across banks of differing sizes.
items.detailed_definition: Base 100 fixes the initial selected year at 100. Subsequent years are computed as (Year Value / Base Value) * 100. This enables direct graphical trajectory comparison between large public and smaller private lenders.
items.formula: Indice Base 100 (t) = (Valeur_t ÷ Valeur_base) × 100
items.interpretation: An index of 135 indicates cumulative growth of +35% since the base year, regardless of initial bank size.
items.example: 2021-2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition (2021 base = 100): In 2024, sector deposits stand at 128.4 (+28.4% cumulative growth).
items.example_vintage: Données 2021-2024, Édition ABIX 2025

items.short_definition: Statistical measurement of the strength and direction of linear association between two financial metrics (-1 to +1).
items.detailed_definition: The Pearson coefficient r ranges from -1 (perfect inverse linear relation) to +1 (perfect positive linear relation), with 0 indicating no linear association. Fundamental ABIX rule: Correlation ≠ Causation. Furthermore, r measures strictly linear relationships and can be sensitive to extreme outliers.
items.formula: r = Σ [ (Xi − X̄)(Yi − Ȳ) ] ÷ [ √Σ(Xi − X̄)² × √Σ(Yi − Ȳ)² ]
items.interpretation: |r| > 0.70 indicates strong linear correlation; 0.40 < |r| < 0.70 moderate; |r| < 0.40 weak or non-linear association.
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition, 20-bank scope: Strong positive linear correlation of r = +0.88 observed between Customer Deposits and Total Assets.
items.abix_benchmark: Forte correlation si |r| >= 0,70 (Seuil d'exclusion multicolinearite ABIX: |r| >= 0,85)
items.example_vintage: Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025, périmètre de 20 banques

items.short_definition: Number of standard deviations separating a bank's metric from the sector mean (or median).
items.detailed_definition: Standardizes metrics to a unitless scale centered at zero. ABIX implements two variants: 1) Classic Z = (X - Mean) / σ; 2) Robust Z = 0.6745 * (X - Median) / MAD. Statistical note: The equivalence of Z = +2 with the top 2.5% holds strictly only under the assumption of a normal distribution.
items.formula: Z classique = (X − X̄) ÷ σ | Z robuste = 0,6745 × (X − Médiane) ÷ MAD
items.interpretation: Z = 0 places the bank at market center. Z > +2 or Z < -2 flags an outlier significantly diverging from sector norms.
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition: A bank with 21.8% ROE against a sector mean of 11.4% (σ = 5.2%) achieves Z = +2.00.
items.example_vintage: Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025, périmètre de 20 banques

items.short_definition: Linear transformation of a financial metric onto a standardized scale from 0 to 100 points.
items.detailed_definition: Projects metrics onto a common 0-100 scale where 100 represents top performance. ABIX scoring rules: 1) Positive direction (higher is better, e.g. ROE, Solvency): Score = [(X - Min)/(Max - Min)] * 100; 2) Inverted direction (lower is better, e.g. CIR, NPL ratio): Score = [(Max - X)/(Max - Min)] * 100. Edge case: If Max equals Min, score defaults to 50.
items.formula: Sens direct : Score = [(X − Min) ÷ (Max − Min)] × 100 | Sens inverse : Score = [(Max − X) ÷ (Max − Min)] × 100
items.interpretation: Enables aggregation and direct comparison of disparate indicators across ABIX dimensional score pillars.
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition, Cost-to-Income (inverted direction): Min = 28.0%, Max = 78.0%. A bank with 38.0% CIR receives a normalized score of [(78.0 - 38.0)/(78.0 - 28.0)] * 100 = 80.0 / 100.
items.abix_benchmark: Score 0 (Pire de la place) à 100 (Leader de la place)
items.example_vintage: Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025, périmètre de 20 banques

items.short_definition: Percentage held by a single bank across an aggregate relative to total consolidated sector volume.
items.detailed_definition: Measures commercial footprint and competitive positioning across financial aggregates (Assets, Deposits, Loans, NBI). ABIX note: Market share is an indicator of relative scale, not an intrinsic measure of profitability or efficiency (contextual reading direction ◆).
items.formula: Part de Marché = (Valeur de la Banque ÷ Total Consolidé du Secteur) × 100
items.interpretation: High market share provides economies of scale, but does not inherently guarantee superior unit profitability.
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition, Total Assets (20 banks): Market leader holds approx. 24.5% market share, with public banks aggregating ~87%.
items.example_vintage: Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025, périmètre de 20 banques

items.short_definition: Absolute difference in percentage points between market share at period t and period t-1.
items.detailed_definition: Measures net competitive momentum and market share shifts among banks. A market share gain indicates the bank outgrew the overall sector on that metric.
items.formula: Δ Part de Marché = Part de Marché_t − Part de Marché_t-1 (en points de pourcentage)
items.interpretation: Sustained share gains reflect aggressive commercial conquest. Share loss indicates commercial slowdown or deliberate de-risking.
items.example: 2024 vs 2023 data, ABIX 2025 edition: A bank expanding loan market share from 3.20% to 3.55% records a net gain of +0.35 pts.
items.example_vintage: Données 2024 vs 2023, Édition ABIX 2025

items.short_definition: Institutional classification of banks according to ownership structure (State-owned vs Private lenders).
items.detailed_definition: Distinguishes the 6 major state-owned commercial banks (plus CNEP-Banque) from the 14 private lenders (international subsidiaries, regional and Islamic banks). Central to ABIX for analyzing structural divergences.
items.formula: Agrégat Public = Σ Banques Publiques | Agrégat Privé = Σ Banques Privées
items.interpretation: Isolates the massive public bank balance sheet dominance (~87%) alongside private banks' relative profitability dynamism.
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition (20 banks): Public sector holds 86.8% of assets and 88.4% of deposits, while private banks generate over 28% of total net income.
items.example_vintage: Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025, périmètre de 20 banques

items.short_definition: Filtering method ensuring only banks with uninterrupted financial reporting across the full timeline are included in multi-year aggregates.
items.detailed_definition: ABIX offers two scope modes: 1) Observed Scope (all reporting banks for a given year); 2) Constant Scope (strictly banks with complete data from start to end year), eliminating distortion in CAGR and Base 100 metrics.
items.formula: Périmètre Constant = { Banques présentes sur chaque année de [Année_début ; Année_fin] }
items.interpretation: Essential for mathematical integrity in multi-year trend analysis, CAGR, and indexed trajectories.
items.example: 2020-2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition: 5-year constant scope retains the 19 continuously active banks, ensuring 100% consistent sector CAGR.
items.example_vintage: Données 2020-2024, Édition ABIX 2025

items.short_definition: Sum of squared market shares of all operating banks, measuring sector concentration on a 0 to 10,000 scale.
items.detailed_definition: HHI squares market shares, placing greater weight on top banks. Standard competitive reading grid (indicative DOJ/FTC benchmarks): 1) HHI < 1,000: Unconcentrated market; 2) 1,000 <= HHI <= 1,800: Moderately concentrated; 3) HHI > 1,800: Highly concentrated. Mandatory ABIX note: These thresholds constitute a standardized competitive analytical grid and do not represent an automatic legal qualification of the Algerian banking market.
items.formula: HHI = Σ (Part de Marché_i)² (pour i = 1 à N banques, parts exprimées en %)
items.interpretation: A high HHI (> 1,800) characterizes an oligopolistic structure where a small group of banks commands the majority of deposits and lending.
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition, Total Assets (20 banks): Sector HHI stands at approx. 1,920 points, characterizing a highly concentrated market by international standards.
items.abix_benchmark: HHI < 1000: Peu concentré | 1000-1800: Modéré | > 1800: Fortement concentré (Grille concurrentielle indicative)
items.example_vintage: Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025, périmètre de 20 banques

items.short_definition: Cumulative market share command held by the top 3 (CR3) or top 5 (CR5) leading banks on a financial metric.
items.detailed_definition: Concentration ratios measure top-tier market command. General definition: CR3 = sum of market shares of the top 3 ranked banks; CR5 = sum of market shares of the top 5 banks for the selected metric and year. ABIX note: Bank rankings are dynamic and computed per year and indicator. Specific bank names appear exclusively in dated historical examples.
items.formula: CR3 = Part_1 + Part_2 + Part_3 | CR5 = Part_1 + Part_2 + Part_3 + Part_4 + Part_5 (parts triées par ordre décroissant)
items.interpretation: CR3 > 50% or CR5 > 70% characterizes a market heavily dominated by a tight leadership cohort.
items.example: Dated example — Total Assets 2024, ABIX 2025 edition (20 banks): Top 3 banks (BEA, BNA, CPA) aggregate a CR3 of 52.4%, and top 5 (with BADR and BDL) reach a CR5 of 74.8%.
items.abix_benchmark: CR3 > 50 %: Forte emprise oligopolistique | CR5 > 70 %: Marché très concentré
items.example_vintage: Exemple daté — Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025, Total Bilan (20 banques)

items.short_definition: Theoretical number of equal-sized banks that would generate the same HHI concentration level observed in the market.
items.detailed_definition: Calculated as 10,000 / HHI. It translates concentration into intuitive terms: in a market with 20 nominal banks, an HHI of 2,000 implies the competitive equivalent of only 5 equal-sized competitors.
items.formula: Nombre Effectif de Banques = 10 000 ÷ HHI
items.interpretation: The wider the gap between nominal and effective bank counts, the more pronounced the market asymmetry and top-bank dominance.
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition, Total Assets (20 nominal banks): With an HHI of 1,920, the effective competitor count is 5.2 equivalent banks.

items.short_definition: Methodological architecture structured across 4 independent analytical pillars: Profitability, Growth & Momentum, Efficiency, and Capitalization.
items.detailed_definition: ABIX 4D Framework assesses banks across four pillars: 1) Profitability (ROE, ROA, Net Margin - 33.3% each); 2) Growth & Momentum (multi-year CAGR across Assets, Loans, NBI, Profit - 25% each); 3) Operational Efficiency (Cost-to-Income, GOI Conversion - 50% each); 4) Accounting Capitalization (Equity/Assets, Equity/Loans - 50% each). Fundamental rule: 4D Framework enforces multidimensional profiling to prevent a single composite score from concealing specific bank vulnerabilities. ABIX explicitly avoids monolithic single ratings.
items.formula: 4 Scores indépendants (0-100) : Score_Rentabilité + Score_Croissance + Score_Efficience + Score_Capitalisation
items.interpretation: Enables radar mapping and positioning matrices to instantly spot structural imbalances (e.g. rapid growth with lagging capital cushion).
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition: A leading private lender exhibiting top Profitability (88/100) and Efficiency (92/100) combined with moderate Growth (64/100).
items.abix_benchmark: Lecture multidimensionnelle par pilier (sans note composite globale artificielle)
items.example_vintage: Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025

items.short_definition: Automated, 100% traceable audit engine identifying trend breaks, balance sheet divergences, and material benchmark gaps.
items.detailed_definition: Deterministic scanning applies transparent, versioned rules (v1.0) directly to financial metrics without black-box modeling. Implemented rules in ABIX: 1) Benchmark gap: absolute gap >= 5.0 pts; 2) Notable annual variation: YoY change >= 15% (or ratio point change >= 5.0 pts); 3) Dimension quartile shift (score change >= 10 pts); 4) Activity divergence alerts: a) Deposits vs Loans growth gap >= 10 pts; b) NBI up >= 15% with Net Profit down <= -10%; c) Assets up >= 10% with ROE down <= -2 pts; d) Net provision surge >= +30%.
items.formula: Règles déterministes d'alerte : |Δ Ratio| ≥ 5 pts | YoY ≥ 15 % | Δ Dépôts − Δ Crédits ≥ 10 pts | Δ Provisions ≥ 30 %
items.interpretation: Guarantees complete mathematical auditability of analytical insights displayed in executive dashboards and bank profiles.
items.example: 2024 data, ABIX 2025 edition: Automatic divergence alert triggered for a bank whose deposits grew +18.5% while loans only expanded +4.2% (gap = 14.3 pts >= 10 pts threshold).
items.abix_benchmark: Règles arithmétiques de détection versionnées v1.0 (100 % traçable)
items.example_vintage: Données 2024, Édition ABIX 2025

items.short_definition: Benchmarking framework evaluating bank digital maturity through auditing mobile apps, web platforms, and e-payment services.
items.detailed_definition: The ABIX E-Banking Barometer is an independent benchmarking tool evaluating digital banking across Algeria. It audits over 40 criteria spanning mobile app functionality, online banking, e-payment capabilities, and UX design.
items.formula: Score E-Banking = Σ (Pondération_dimension × Score_dimension) (sur une échelle normalisée de 0 à 100)
items.interpretation: A top score reflects a mature, seamless, and secure digital banking offering for retail and corporate clients.
items.example: ABIX Barometer 2025 edition: Bank scores ranging from 32/100 (basic features) to over 86/100 for leading digital pioneers.
items.abix_benchmark: Score 0-100 normalisé sur grille multicritère auditée
